Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Demarcation & ownership clarification (Dedicated vs Private VPC)

Hi Thomas — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our demo and the things we agreed to validate for MedSys: 

1) High-level ask we heard
- You want strong data isolation guarantees for PHI workflows and would prefer a model where control-plane residency and key ownership are under your control if possible.

2) Points we agreed to follow up on (items below need confirmation from you so we can scope):
- Control plane residency: Do you require the control plane (API endpoint/configuration plane) to live inside your VPC/on-prem, or is a customer-isolated Dedicated GPU pool with strict egress controls acceptable?
- Key management: BYOK with HSM-backed KMS vs Redwood-managed keys — which is mandatory vs preferred?
- Network isolation: VPC peering & private peering, VPN-only access, or do you need an air-gapped on-prem variant?
- Audit & retention: Minimum audit log retention window and whether logs must be stored in your S3/KMS.
- Model pinning & image custody: Need to know whether you require us to pin model binaries in a customer-controlled registry.

3) What Redwood can do (brief):
- Dedicated: Dedicated GPU pools and tenant isolation at the serving layer; control plane remains Redwood-managed (we provide hardened endpoints + strict ACLs and no noisy-neighbor compute).
- Private VPC / On-prem: Customer-managed control plane (VPC), optional on-prem package, BYOK/HSM integrations, full network control and egress policy enforcement.

Attachments: redwood-segmentation-exec-summary.pdf (short exec summary of Dedicated vs Private), redwood-soc2-highlights.pdf (SOC2 high-level evidence).

Next steps: Please confirm the three must-haves for MedSys from the bullets above (control plane residency, key ownership, and network isolation). Once you confirm, Ben / I will schedule a short security deep-dive with our Solutions & Security engineers and provide a preliminary cost delta and timeline for a Private VPC/on-prem engagement.

Regards,
Priya
Account Exec | Redwood Inference

From: Thomas Reed <thomas.reed@medsys.com>

Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Demarcation & ownership clarification (Dedicated vs Private VPC)

Thanks Priya — great demo. A few clarifications from our side so you can scope accurately: 

- Control plane residency: For PHI workloads we need the control plane to be resident in our VPC or on-prem. Dedicated pools are fine for compute isolation, but the management/control plane must be customer-managed for our legal and audit posture.
- Key management: BYOK is mandatory for anything that touches cardholder / patient identifiers. We require HSM-backed KMS (Cloud HSM or on-prem HSM) and cryptographic custody under our policy.
- Network isolation: VPC peering or private interconnect is acceptable; however we cannot accept outbound egress to public internet for model artifacts or logs. We need either private peering + egress block or an on-prem variant.
- Audit logs: 7 years retention for specific event types (access, model invocation metadata). If logs can be pushed to our S3 with our KMS, that is preferred.
- Timeline & cost: Looking for directional cost delta between (1) Dedicated with strict egress + Redwood-managed control plane + integration for logs to our S3, (2) Private VPC with BYOK, (3) On-prem. Rough order magnitudes are fine for now.

Also copy from procurement (procure@medsys.com) — they'll need an initial SOW checklist and any standard MSA redlines you anticipate.

- Thomas
Director, Cloud Security | MedSys Health

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Thomas Reed <thomas.reed@medsys.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procure@medsys.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Demarcation & ownership clarification (Dedicated vs Private VPC)

Thomas — thanks, really helpful list. Below are clarifications and proposed next steps based on each of your bullets: 

Control plane residency
- Confirmed: Dedicated pools do not move the Redwood control plane into your VPC. Dedicated gives isolated serving resources and stricter tenant separation, but control plane services (config, routing, rollout) remain Redwood-managed.
- Private VPC / On-prem: we offer a Private control plane deployment where the control plane lives in your VPC (or on-prem) and we provide the runtime as a set of customer-controlled services. This is the option that meets your "must have" control-plane residency requirement.

Key management (BYOK)
- BYOK + HSM: Supported in Private VPC and on-prem deployments. We support Cloud HSM integrations (AWS CloudHSM, Azure Dedicated HSM) and HSM-backed KMS for key custody.
- Dedicated: Redwood-managed KMS is the default; we can discuss a hybrid where customer KMS wraps tokens for certain artifacts, but full HSM-backed BYOK is only available with Private.

Network isolation & egress
- Private VPC: allows VPC peering / private interconnect. Egress can be fully controlled (block public egress for artifacts/logs).
- Dedicated: we can implement strict egress filtering and private peering options, but there are limitations versus a full Private deployment — we need to enumerate which artifacts/logs we can guarantee never leave your network under Dedicated.

Audit logs & retention
- We can ship audit logs to your S3 with your KMS in Private and on-prem deployments. For Dedicated we can provide secure log-forwarding; retention windows beyond 1 year will need an explicit storage SOW (we can estimate cost).

Cost & timeline (directional)
- I'll pull a rough delta: Dedicated (isolation + egress controls) = baseline + modest premium; Private VPC (BYOK + control-plane residency) = higher one-time setup + monthly infra; On-prem = highest setup + ops consulting. Ben will include more concrete ranges in the follow-up.

Next steps
- Proposal: Security deep-dive (45m) with our Solutions Engineer + Security Engineering. Can we do Thu 6/25 10am ET or Fri 6/26 1pm ET?
- I will attach the short SOC2 highlights and segmentation exec summary (attached). Ben will follow with cost-deltas and a preliminary SOW checklist for procurement.

Regards,
Priya
